findings.title: Logged-in user A can delete user B's rows in public.drafts
findings.fix: Scope the DELETE policy on public.drafts to the caller. A DELETE policy must never be wider than the SELECT policy.

findings.title: Logged-in user A and an anonymous visitor can delete user B's rows in public.note_attachments
findings.fix: Scope the DELETE policy on public.note_attachments to the caller. A DELETE policy must never be wider than the SELECT policy.

findings.title: Logged-in user A and an anonymous visitor can insert rows into public.note_attachments that are attributed to user B

A.result: row passed the authorization check; only constraint 23505 stopped it (the probe replays an existing row)

anon.result: row passed the authorization check; only constraint 23505 stopped it (the probe replays an existing row)

findings.fix: Add WITH CHECK to the INSERT policy on public.note_attachments so the owner must be auth.uid().

findings.title: Logged-in user A and an anonymous visitor can read rows in public.invoice_summary that belong only to user B
findings.fix: Make the view respect the caller's row access: ALTER VIEW public.invoice_summary SET (security_invoker = true);

findings.title: Logged-in user A and an anonymous visitor can read rows in public.note_attachments that belong only to user B
findings.fix: Scope the SELECT policy on public.note_attachments to the caller, for example USING (user_id = auth.uid()). If RLS is off, turn it on first.

findings.title: Logged-in user A and an anonymous visitor can update user B's rows in public.note_attachments
findings.fix: Scope the UPDATE policy on public.note_attachments with both USING and WITH CHECK tied to the caller.

findings.title: Logged-in user A can update user B's rows in public.profiles
findings.fix: Scope the UPDATE policy on public.profiles with both USING and WITH CHECK tied to the caller.

findings.title: Logged-in user A and an anonymous visitor can read user B's data by calling public.get_notes_for(p_user_id uuid)
findings.fix: Inside public.get_notes_for(p_user_id uuid), take the identity from auth.uid() instead of an argument, or raise when they differ.

findings.title: Logged-in user A and an anonymous visitor can change user B's rows by calling public.delete_note(p_note_id uuid)
findings.fix: Inside public.delete_note(p_note_id uuid), verify the row belongs to auth.uid() before changing it (add "AND user_id = auth.uid()").

personas: User A, after editing their own user_metadata
findings.title: Editing their own user_metadata lets user A read user B's rows in public.support_tickets
findings.fix: Do not use user_metadata in access rules; users can change it themselves. Use app_metadata or a roles table.

findings.title: SECURITY DEFINER function public.get_notes_for(p_user_id uuid) takes a user id from the caller and never checks who is calling
findings.fix:
Take the identity from the session, not from an argument:
--   ... WHERE user_id = auth.uid()
-- or reject mismatches at the top of the function:
--   IF p_user_id IS DISTINCT FROM auth.uid() THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'not allowed'; END IF;

findings.title: Policy "drafts_cleanup" on public.drafts allows DELETE on every row for authenticated
findings.fix:
ALTER POLICY "drafts_cleanup" ON public.drafts
  USING (user_id = auth.uid()) WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid());  -- use the table's real owner column

findings.title: Policy "profiles_update" on public.profiles allows UPDATE on every row for authenticated
findings.fix:
ALTER POLICY "profiles_update" ON public.profiles
  USING (user_id = auth.uid()) WITH CHECK (user_id = auth.uid());  -- use the table's real owner column

findings.title: Policy "tickets_read" on public.support_tickets trusts user_metadata, which every user can edit for themselves
findings.fix:
Read roles from app_metadata (server-controlled) or from a roles table:
-- (auth.jwt() -> 'app_metadata' ->> 'role') = 'support'

findings.title: Row Level Security is off on public.note_attachments and the API roles can reach it
View public.invoice_summary runs with its owner's rights, so RLS on the tables underneath is skipped
findings.fix: ALTER VIEW public.invoice_summary SET (security_invoker = true);

findings.title: SECURITY DEFINER function public.delete_note(p_note_id uuid) can be called without logging in
findings.fix:
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.delete_note(p_note_id uuid) FROM PUBLIC, anon;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.delete_note(p_note_id uuid) TO authenticated;

findings.title: SECURITY DEFINER function public.get_notes_for(p_user_id uuid) can be called without logging in
findings.fix:
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.get_notes_for(p_user_id uuid) FROM PUBLIC, anon;
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION public.get_notes_for(p_user_id uuid) TO authenticated;

findings.title: SECURITY DEFINER function public.delete_note(p_note_id uuid) has no fixed search_path
findings.fix:
ALTER FUNCTION public.delete_note(p_note_id uuid) SET search_path = '';
-- and schema-qualify every object the function touches.

findings.title: SECURITY DEFINER function public.get_notes_for(p_user_id uuid) has no fixed search_path
findings.fix:
ALTER FUNCTION public.get_notes_for(p_user_id uuid) SET search_path = '';
-- and schema-qualify every object the function touches.

accepted.title: Logged-in user A can read rows in public.profiles that belong only to user B
accepted.fix: Scope the SELECT policy on public.profiles to the caller, for example USING (user_id = auth.uid()). If RLS is off, turn it on first.
accepted.accepted_reason: Profiles are public to logged-in users by design (display name and bio only).

accepted.title: Policy "plans_read" on public.plans lets every anon/authenticated caller read every row
accepted.fix:
If the table is public by design, accept this finding with a reason. Otherwise scope it:
-- ALTER POLICY "plans_read" ON public.plans USING (user_id = auth.uid());

accepted.title: Policy "profiles_read" on public.profiles lets every authenticated caller read every row
accepted.fix:
If the table is public by design, accept this finding with a reason. Otherwise scope it:
-- ALTER POLICY "profiles_read" ON public.profiles USING (user_id = auth.uid());
accepted.accepted_reason: Same decision: profiles are readable by every logged-in user.
